tldr: We establish matching finite-sample rates for pure-private global zero-CATE detection, supremum recovery, and finite-honest simultaneous maximum band width on the fixed binary observational class. With \(m=n\epsilon\), \(\mathcal L=\log(\exp(1)+n)\), and \(\ell=\log(\exp(1)+m)\), testing has rate \(\min\{1,\max((\mathcal L/n^2)^{1/8},(nm)^{-1/7},m^{-1/2})\}\), while curve release and bands share \(\min\{1,\max((\mathcal L/n^2)^{1/8},(\ell/(nm))^{1/7},(\ell/m)^{1/2})\}\). Total original-record mechanisms attain these rates, direct spatial converses prove them, and the exact elbows characterize when release and bands are logarithmically harder than testing.
gap: Private conditional-independence testing supplies adjusted screens under regression-error or model-X conditions, and approximate-private CATE learning supplies functional releases. Neither verified source supplies a pure-private, all-budget matched global-test, supremum-risk and finite-honest maximum-width frontier on \(\mathcal M\). The accepted internal point-parent resolves a single location; it supplies neither exponential spatial calibration nor a multi-location band converse.
